co_air_force_academy.blurb: Just north of Colorado Springs, the Academy's climbing is a scattering of small areas rather than one big crag. Mt. Ansel holds most of the bouldering, with problems from V0 to V7, while Stanley Canyon and Eagle's Peak carry the sport and trad lines, mostly 5.8 to 5.12 with a few easier ones. Stanley Canyon is a steep canyon on the Rampart Range, and its rock is granite that can be slick in winter or when wet. Smaller outliers such as Mt. Harmon and West Monument Creek add a handful of top-rope and trad routes, so expect variety more than volume.

al_moss_rock_preserve.blurb: A city-run nature preserve in Hoover, on the edge of the Birmingham area, Moss Rock is almost purely a bouldering destination. The problems sit on sandstone blocks in a wooded setting that feels wilder than its suburban surroundings. The grades start with plenty of easy V0 to V2 climbs, thin out through the middle grades, and reach a handful in the double digits. Styles vary: sloping mantles, balance moves on small crimps, overhangs, roofs and a few highballs, all on coarse rock that grips well. Grass Man Area and Ozzy Area hold the most problems, with smaller groups such as Lost Roof Area and Novak Area spread around them.

ca_14_whitney_surrounding_peaks.blurb: On the east side of the High Sierra above the town of Lone Pine, this group of peaks centers on Mt. Whitney and takes in Lone Pine Peak, Mt. Russell and Keeler Needle, among many others. It is mountain terrain rather than crag climbing: alpine routes dominate, alongside scrambles from class 1 to class 4, some traditional rock lines, a few mixed and ice routes and a small amount of bouldering near Lower Boy Scout Lake. Technical rock grades run mostly from 5.8 to 5.11, with a few harder lines. Mt. Whitney itself is Cretaceous granite and rises steeply from the Owens Valley, with a much gentler western side.

ca_nut_tree_boulders_the.blurb: Basalt boulders scattered over rolling open-space hills above Vacaville, midway between Sacramento and the Bay Area. This is bouldering only, in three clusters: Boxcar Woody Boulders sit beside the road, Hillcrest Boulders are more spread out, and Woodcrest Boulders are the most concentrated and suit circuits. Most boulders stand 10 to 20 feet tall, with a few highballs near 30 feet. The problems lean easy to moderate, with a good spread from V0 to V5 and only a few climbs at V7 to V9. Winter is the best season, cooler spring and fall days also work, and summer is usually too hot. The basalt turns fragile when wet.
